Under the Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), in force 2025-04-26, Clause 3.1, to test a shuttle a player uses a full underhand stroke which makes contact with the shuttle over the back boundary line, and the shuttle is hit at an upward angle and in a direction parallel to the side lines. Under Clause 3.2, a shuttle of correct speed will land not less than 530 mm and not more than 990 mm short of the other back boundary line as in Diagram B. In addition, under the Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), in force 2025-04-26, Clause 3.6.3, the Referee at all times, when observing play, considers whether the shuttle speed selected before play started still appears to be correct.
Diagram B (Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2)) is the diagram showing where a correctly sped shuttle lands. The ITTO 7.0 (5) clauses 3.5.4.4–3.5.4.6 concern the Referee's handling of the shuttle-speed decision: when assessing the test result, take into account how the shuttles were hit (strength of shot and trajectory) and whether they were hit from the correct location over the back line (Law 3); communicate the shuttle speed decision to Shuttle Control; and do not communicate the decision to the shuttle tester or ask his opinion.
